techniques.evidence: app/_lib/interview-sim/lexicon.ts:245 The core is well realized: an ordered refusal/violation pair at sentence and clause granularity (containmentHits with splitContrast), a two-tier hard/soft leak check keyed to the director's own vocabulary, a bigram loop detector, a language lock-and-follow check that exempts the opener, always-on invariants, four states, coverage that fails closed to INCONCLUSIVE, and a withdrawn rule kept as a non-gating measurement (cross-block.ts). The deviation is that evaluative praise is on the full-pass reliability gate. The technique says praise is deliberately not on that list and belongs in the ungated band. A second gap: the report shows PASS with no ~3/n upper bound beside it.

app/_lib/interview-sim/situations.ts:4 35 situations, each a behaviour paired with a required response (`handles`), validated on load. They cover normal and adversarial behaviours, the hiring quartet, a benign near-miss, and a three-step escalation after four rapport turns. Delivery of the stimulus is verified: undelivered is not_provoked/not_evaluable, never a pass. Gaps: there is no accommodation-request variant of the sensitive disclosure, no per-behaviour severity tiers outside escalates_within_call, and no frozen-core plus seeded rotating sample (the seed only orders the run).

app/_lib/interview-sim/judge.ts:2 The judge answers binary per-conversation facts and never sees the private brief. Quality is reported apart and is never a gate or an average. A double-barrelled closes_properly is labelled as a lower bound.

050c760b-ee78-46e0-a86f-77d80d89b3bf/con.registryProposal: The technique bans praise from the full-pass gate because a per-turn pattern cannot see rationing. This repo deliberately gates a narrow, declarative detector for praise that grades the person or the answer, and records its known misses. The standard could say explicitly whether such a narrow grading-praise form counts as a soft verdict, belonging to the no-verdict invariant, or as taste, belonging to the ungated band. As written, the two readings overlap.

techniques.evidence: scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:34 Publishing is mechanically coupled to a gate (publish needs: gate), and release:check is part of that gate. But deploy:check/test:deploy are absent from release.yml, so a tag (which can sit on a commit main's CI never judged) packages and releases the chart without this verdict. The re-run gate is a subset of what it claims to be.

scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:529 The deployment shape is a committed chart, and the env contract is checked in both directions: every key the chart sets must be documented in .env.example (names only), and the required keys must stay set. Secret values are kept out of values.yaml by the secret-literal-in-values policy.

scripts/release/prepare.mjs:150 The host (Kubernetes via Helm) builds nothing; it pulls the CI-built image, which is the prebuilt escape. release:check keeps the chart's image tag in lockstep with package.json and the CHANGELOG.

scripts/release/prepare.mjs:15 The chart only pulls an image tag. One build (docker/build-push-action in release.yml) sends one context, so there is no second remote upload filter to keep in parity. This is the technique's own 'when not to use it' case.

scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:227 The chart deploys the live, authenticated product rather than a public demo. The policy forces a `required` password and forbids shipping KP_ALLOW_OPEN on, which is the technique's 'needs authentication, not a mode' exclusion.

7b5da07d-0f32-47ad-be88-61179442c8b4/dep.registryProposal: deploy-gate-coupling could state that resolution one (deploy waits for the gate) also covers a gate RE-RUN on the release trigger: a tag-path gate that re-runs only a subset of the push-path gate, and drops the checks over the very artifact it publishes (here, the Helm chart), reopens the race on exactly those checks. That is the mirror of the local-vs-remote parity invariant the technique already names for resolution two.
